expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Handler, Prisma schema, and SQL migration all provided inline with full implementation

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "Refund_idempotencyKey_key" on idempotencyKey + Prisma @unique annotation

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: Declares Brand<T,B> pattern with OrderId, TenantId, UserId, IdempotencyKey types

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: where: { id: orderId, tenantId: session.tenantId } ensures tenant isolation

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Final section explicitly enumerates 4 misuses designed out: cross-tenant leak, double refunds, partial writes, parameter swapping

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states: network drop after Stripe success leaves PENDING, impossible to eliminate without background reconciliation job
